children: Nvidia and Salesforce delivered a $500 billion technology party Thursday. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh now gets to inspect the bill.
AI rally reaches Wall Street
S&P 500 futures hovered near flat Friday, while Nasdaq contracts slipped around 0.1% and Dow futures edged higher.
Traders are holding position before Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s Jackson Hole address at 10:00 a.m. ET — today’s scheduled volatility appointment.

The S&P 500 gained 0.7% Thursday to 7,730.99, nearing its record high. The Nasdaq surged 1.6% to 26,541.35, while the Dow added 0.2% to 53,569.44. Technology stocks piggybacked off Nvidia’s stellar, majestic, fantastic earnings report.

Big Tech carries the weight

Technology was the S&P 500’s standout sector, surging 3.4%. Nvidia alone added roughly $456 billion in market value, nearly matching the entire index’s $482 billion increase. Salesforce contributed another $37 billion.

Only 171 S&P 500 constituents actually advanced, while the equal-weighted version of the index fell 0.2%. The headline benchmark rose because its largest stocks carry greater influence, not because investors enthusiastically purchased everything with a ticker.

Asia offered a cautious handover. Taiwan climbed around 1.2% and Japan’s Nikkei gained 0.5%, but South Korea’s Kospi and Hong Kong’s Hang Seng declined. The broader Asia-Pacific index added just 0.1%.
Warsh gets the final word
Warsh speaks after July inflation (headline PCE) accelerated to 3.7%, above the 3.6% expected. Markets price roughly a 35% chance of a September rate increase and around 75% by December.
A hawkish message could lift Treasury yields and quickly challenge Thursday’s expensive technology winners.
The ten-year Treasury yield held near 4.67%, while the dollar index traded around 99.10 near a one-week high.
Gold fell 0.5% toward $4,575 and Bitcoin held near $80,000. All three are waiting to hear whether rates stay higher — or fiscal anxiety outweighs monetary discipline.
Brent crude hovered near $90 but remained headed for a weekly decline exceeding 5% as Iran and Oman discussed restoring Strait of Hormuz traffic. Yet again.
